A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLM Data Auditor survey despite the changed title. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: Tables 2–7 contain the authors' original categorical analysis of evaluation coverage in selected publications. This constitutes literature-data analysis; the survey does not report original model-training experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains and extends the authors' literature audit, reporting sample-specific findings such as fairness coverage in two of seven tabular works. Section 10 distinguishes this analytical synthesis from end-to-end empirical validation on synthetic data.

M1.justification: The paper remains a survey and evaluation taxonomy, without a revised generation algorithm, model, training objective, or inference procedure. Newly reviewed methods and expanded metric descriptions do not establish changes to an implemented method.

E1.justification: The audit retains the same six modalities. Newly discussed benchmarks and generation methods are literature sources, not additional datasets or task scenarios experimentally evaluated by the authors; changes to the audited sample belong to E3.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates benchmark baselines against a proposed computational method. Audit-table membership changes are literature-analysis changes. The PMI-FAITH entry renamed PMI-DECODE in Table 2 refers to the same Nandwani et al. work.

E3.justification: The literature-audit samples change in Tables 2–5 and 7, while contamination coding is added to Tables 2–3 and diversity coding to Tables 3 and 5. The three-level coverage scheme remains. Section 1.1 mainly documents selection and coding practices; it does not establish changed model-training settings.

E4.justification: Neither version supplies original ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or error-analysis experiments. The new cross-modal synthesis in Section 8 interprets the survey's evaluation dimensions rather than reporting additional experimental tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, significance tests, or annotator-agreement estimates for its own audit. v3's explicit sample counts and representativeness qualifications do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The audit evidence gains new rows and evaluated dimensions across several modalities, including contamination findings in Tables 2–3. Table 4 removes TabSyn and adds UDF-MIX, FairCauseSyn, and AIGT: explicit fairness coverage changes from zero of five to two of seven, while explicit diversity coverage disappears with TabSyn's removal. These are findings under revised selections, not same-setting performance changes; retained coverage ratings largely remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds mathematical definitions for survey-level overlap and contamination rates, a cutoff-related performance gap, and reasoning-trajectory diversity in Sections 2.3, 3.2, and 3.3. These are limited formal additions without new theorems or proofs. Appendix A's notation content is retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a two-pillar, six-modality evaluation survey. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion narrow broad evaluation-gap claims to under-covered dimensions within the representative sample, and benchmark contamination becomes an explicitly advertised taxonomy dimension.

C2.justification: New Section 8 distinguishes foundational, transferable, and modality-concentrated evaluation dimensions and explains why shared concerns require different operationalizations. Section 1.1 explicitly rejects field-wide prevalence interpretations, and Section 10 clarifies that the framework lacks end-to-end empirical validation. These substantially refine applicability and interpretation.

D1.justification: Section 1.1 newly explains family-based paper selection, five functional roles, and coverage-coding criteria. The abstract replaces the anonymous repository address with a named GitHub repository address. These improve documented audit and access information without establishing new computational implementation details.

R1.justification: The survey substantially expands its treatment of contamination detection and contamination-aware benchmarking, reasoning and structured-output diversity, and fairness-aware tabular generation. Added discussions include DyCodeEval, FairCauseSyn, UDF-MIX, and automata-based steering. Appendix B retains the same substantive comparison with earlier surveys.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title, extensively revises metric descriptions from experiment-like first-person statements to survey explanations, and rewrites gap discussions around explicit sample counts. It adds dedicated audit-protocol and cross-modal-synthesis sections; the existing future-directions section is retained and renumbered.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are substantially redrawn. Tables 2–7 gain Family and Role columns, several gain additional coverage columns and rows, and new Table 8 presents cross-modal synthesis. Captions and table layouts are revised throughout; the appendix tables are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the survey more transparent and useful through explicit audit criteria, appropriately bounded gap claims, expanded contamination and diversity coverage, and cross-modal interpretation. These improve synthesis and evidential clarity while most retained audit judgments and the central contribution remain stable. The revised counts reflect changed literature samples, not demonstrated improvements in synthetic-data performance.
